book.principiamagica.principia.golemancy: Once dried, an axiom is given to a golem with a right-click. See [Purpose](entry://principiamagica:principia/golemancy/purpose).

The scribe calls them *me*. I call them axioms: laws that need no proof, only obedience. Carve the purpose while the clay is wet, with something of that purpose pressed in: grain for the harvest, a sapling for the felling. Then steep it in its matter and dry it in the light. Wet clay can still be persuaded. Dried clay keeps its law.

*Enki kept the decrees in his house in Eridu: the decree of the plough, the decree of the axe, the decree of kingship, the decree of the destruction of cities. Each could be held in the hand. Each could be given away.*
A golem carries two items: one in its hand and one on its back. Both are kept when the golem is picked up with the stylus.

Right-click one of your golems with the imprint tablet to copy its work zones and container links. Right-click another of your golems to paste them there.
\
\
The copy is stored relative to the golem's anchor, so it lands in the same place around the new golem. Crouch-right-click the tablet to clear the copy.

Right-click a hurt golem with quickened clay. Each clay heals one health. A golem at full health is not affected, so its other interactions still work.
\
\
Creative players keep their clay.
A hurt golem can be mended with quickened clay. When it has to move, I can pick it up with the stylus and set it down elsewhere, and it keeps everything it was given.

Crouch-left-click a golem with the stylus to pick it up. It becomes a golem item again, and it keeps its work zone, its inventory and its equipment. Nothing drops. Placing the item restores all of it.
*Flesh that is torn must be mended with flesh. The clay that holds the body will take the mending, and the body will stand again.*
Golems are clay that has been given flesh and then a purpose. The first pages are about the body, the rest about the law that moves it.
*Wet clay is open. It takes the word and the thumbprint and the fly that lands on it. Do not let it hear what you do not mean.*

Only natural trees are felled. A tree counts as natural when its logs touch leaves that are decaying. Player-built wood is never touched, and trees spreading more than 10 blocks sideways or taller than 48 blocks are left alone.
\
\
A better axe chops faster.
The Axiom of Felling sets a golem to the trees. It fells from the stump upward, chops each log with its axe, and replants a sapling on every stump it has one for.

**Replant saplings**: plant a sapling on each felled stump.
\
\
**Clear blocking leaves**: break natural leaves that wall in a trunk at stump height. Leaves that a player placed are never broken.
\
\
**Apply bone meal to saplings**: help the saplings in the zone grow.
\
\
**Pick up stray items**: collect the logs, saplings and sticks that lie in the zone.
*The tree was grown to be cut, and the gods allow it to be cut. Let the axe find the trees that are no longer needed, and leave the wood that was built by hands where it stands.*
The Axiom of Harvest sets a golem to the field. It cuts ripe crops, replants them from the seeds it carries, and fetches seeds from supply chests when it runs short.

**Replant crops**: sow the field again after the harvest.
\
\
**Clear obstructions**: remove grass, flowers and similar from the work zone.
\
\
**Till soil near water**: turn the soil with a hoe, if the golem carries one.
\
\
**Apply bone meal**: help crops grow.
\
\
**Pick up stray items**: collect what lies in the field.
*Let the grain stand where the law says, and let it be cut when it is ripe. Let the field be sown again before the sun has moved.*

Right-click a block face with the stylus to carve the first corner. Right-click a second face to carve the opposite corner. Together the two glyphs mark a rectangle, no wider, deeper, or taller than 64 blocks. You can carve multiple overlapping boundaries, as long as no two corners occupy the same block.

Shift-right-click a carved glyph or anywhere on a boundary box with the stylus to erase it, and the field it belonged to is gone. You can do this from a distance: aim at a glyph or box and it highlights, then shift-right-click to erase. Breaking the block a glyph is carved into does not erase it.

With your golem selected, right-click a chest with the stylus to link it. Each further right-click changes the link: supply, then deposit, then both, then unlinked again. A supply chest gives the golem seeds, saplings and bone meal. A deposit chest takes the harvest. Shift-right-click a linked chest to remove its link at once, and the boundary around it stays as it is.
The chests touching the golem when it is given an axiom are linked both ways, so a golem placed beside its field and a chest works right away.
A chest is only a chest until the golem knows what to do with it. Let it fetch from one, and let it fill another. I do not need to touch either myself.

Aim at a boundary box and hold shift while scrolling to move all of it up or down at once. Its corners keep their blocks and move with it, as long as they do not collide with another corner. A flat boundary stays flat, and the golem decides how far it reaches from its level.

The old landholders carved their boundaries in stone and cursed whoever moved them. My golem needs only the marks. Carved corners tell it where its field begins and ends; it decides how high to reach unless I lift the boundary myself.

Hold shift and scroll over a corner glyph with the stylus to lift or lower that corner along its plumb line, up to the 64-block boundary height limit. When the corners sit at different heights, the boundary is a box, and the golem works the whole box, reaching as far as its axiom allows.
*This is the boundary of the field. Whoever moves this stone, whoever says "the field is not bounded", may the gods of the land curse him, may his name be torn out.*
Right-click your golem with the stylus to select it. Right-click it again to deselect it. Only the selected golem shows its boundaries while you hold the stylus.
Hold an axiom and right-click your golem. The axiom sinks into the clay and is spent. A golem that holds an axiom is no longer purposeless: it sets to work at once.

**Work** makes the golem do its job inside its work area.
\
\
**Follow** makes it walk after you.
\
\
**Stay** keeps it in place. A golem without an axiom can only follow or stay.
I pressed the axiom against its chest and the clay took it like a mouth. It went to the field at once. It has not looked at me since.

Shift-right-click your golem with an empty hand, or remove the axiom in its screen. The axiom returns to your hands and the golem is purposeless again. It stays where it is, unless it was set to follow you.
Right-click your golem with an empty hand to open its screen. There you set its mode, its work area and its links to containers.
*Let him bear the toil of the gods. Let him bear the basket.*

Without a work area of its own, a golem given an axiom marks a field of nine by nine blocks around the spot where it stands, one block down and two up. Containers touching the golem are linked to it and serve as both supply and deposit.
\
\
A field and a chest beside the golem are enough. A work area you have already set up is kept.
Wood for the bones, quickened clay for the sinews. When I set it down it turned its head toward me. Nothing more. It does not know what it is for. It only knows that I am here.

Place the golem on a block face and it stands there for good. It never wanders off and it never fades.
\
\
Without an axiom it has no purpose. It stays where it is put, or follows you if you ask it to. It cannot work until it is given an axiom.
*Fourteen pieces of clay she pinched off. Seven on the right, seven on the left. Between them she set the brick.*
book.principiamagica.principia.khemeia.d: A curing step takes 25 mB of each Primal in a pair and gives back 25 mB of the compound. The Steeping Jar does this on its own. Unguent is the one I need for quickened clay.
*Mire, bitumen, unguent, kohl. The tablets call them the blacks of the dead. Each is two Primals made one, and each is made only in the dark.*
The steeped axioms are dried here, and their recipes are shown with the rest of the axiom pipeline. See [Processing Axioms](entry://principiamagica:principia/golemancy/axioms).

Only steeped unfired axioms can go in the input. Each tick the drying moves forward by the light level divided by 15. At full light a finished axiom takes 400 ticks (20 seconds). Drying pauses while the output has no room.
\
\
An empty hand takes the output first. Taking the input back out restarts its drying.

Put a steeped axiom into the input and take the finished axiom from the output. Drying runs on the light at the block above the slab, so a lamp or the open sky dries it. In the dark it does not dry at all.
*The clay dries in the sun, and the law dries with it. Left in the dark, the clay stays soft, and the law is not yet bound.*
book.principiamagica.principia.khemeia.k: Every change I make in these vessels is a process, and the copied tablets call them all khemeia. Libation washes the Primals out of things. The basin and the jar cure pairs of them into compounds. The trough steeps. The slab dries. I will set down each one as I learn it.

**Libation**: washing offerings with water on the Libation Slab.
\
\
**Curing**: pairs of Primals cure into compounds in the Wabet Basin (light) and the Steeping Jar (dark).
\
\
**Steeping**: items take Principles in the Catch Trough and become something new.
\
\
**Drying**: steeped items dry on the Drying Slab into finished work.
*The flood leaves black silt on the banks. The scribes of the Black Land learned to ask the silt for more than it gave, and they named the craft after the earth itself: khemeia.*
book.principiamagica.principia.khemeia.l: Loam and shard are what the axes of the harvest and the felling need. Myrrh and glaze I have not yet found a use for, but I will write them down all the same.
*Loam is the earth the harvest grows in, and shard is the stone the axe is set in. The sun-court made them both. The law is given its purpose through them.*
I cannot make them yet, and I do not know what they are for. I will write down whatever I learn of them here, and nothing I have not yet seen.

*Beyond the black and the light the tablets name further waters, eight of them, mixed from what the Primals and the compounds already give. The scribe wrote their names and left the rest of the recipe blank.*
book.principiamagica.principia.khemeia.s: An item in the Catch Trough and the Principles its recipe asks for. After 100 ticks the item is replaced, and exactly those Principles are used up. The rest stays in the trough. If the Principles fall short, or the item stops matching, the progress starts again.
*The tablets say the black water changes what it touches. A thing set in the trough, and given the water it asks for, comes out as something else.*

Steeped clay becomes [Quickened Clay](entry://principiamagica:principia/scribes_path/quickened_clay). A steeped unfired axiom is dried on the Drying Slab, see [Processing Axioms](entry://principiamagica:principia/golemancy/axioms).
A clay jar with a brick belly and a lid that stays down while it works. Fill it from the libation spouts and it takes the Primals. Dark compounds form inside, and I do not need to tend it.
*The jar is closed with its lid, and the tablets say why. What is cured in the dark must not be seen while it works. Keep it shut, and let the dark do its labour.*

The jar holds 1000 mB of Principles and takes them whenever it has room. It is filled the same way as the Wabet Basin: from libation spouts, or by pouring a clay phial into it.
\
\
Each pair of Primals cures into its dark compound, 25 mB and 25 mB into 25 mB, and each step takes 160 ticks. Open the Vessel Tap to drain the jar into the block below it. Curing continues while it drains.
book.principiamagica.principia.khemeia.w:
The basin needs a light level of at least 9 at its own block. Below that, nothing cures and the Primals wait in the water.
\
\
At full light a step takes 100 ticks (5 seconds). The dimmer the light, the longer it takes. Each step uses 25 mB of each Primal in a pair and gives 25 mB of the compound.
\
\
The basin holds 1000 mB, and the Vessel Tap drains it into the block below.

Libation spouts drain into the basin and the Primals mix in it. Pairs cure into light compounds, but only in light. The brighter it is, the faster they cure. When the compounds are ready I open the tap, and they run into the trough below.
*The pure place is an open court, and the offerings are laid out where the sun can reach them. The tablets say the sun binds what the hand cannot.*
book.principiamagica.principia.name: Principia
book.principiamagica.principia.scribes_p: The trough holds one item and up to 500 mB of Principles. It takes only items that a steeping recipe uses, and an empty hand takes the item back out. Breaking it keeps its Principles on the dropped block. How the trough steeps is described in [Steeping](entry://principiamagica:principia/khemeia/steeping).
A clay trough set in front of the spout, where the run-off collects. It is where the water's Principles meet what I put in it.
*The trough takes the run-off, and in the run-off the clay listens. Let it hold one thing at a time, and let that thing be changed.*
Clay that has drunk the flesh can be given a purpose. The pages on the golems are gathered in [Golemancy](category://principiamagica:principia/golemancy).
Everything the vessels do, the copied tablets call khemeia. The processes are gathered in a separate set of pages: [Khemeia](category://principiamagica:principia/khemeia).
An offering table with a carved spout, like the ones in the temples. I set things on it and pour water over them, and what the water takes from them is what I am after.
*They set the bread and the beer on the stone, and the priest poured the water after them. The gods took the essence of the offering, and the stone kept the rest.*

Right-click the slab with an item that can be washed to put it on the slab, as much as fits. An empty hand takes the stack back, unless an item is already dissolving.
\
\
Pour water in with a bucket or any water container, up to 1000 mB. Each item dissolves one at a time, in 40 ticks, and only while the water covers its full cost. Its Principles go into the slab's storage.
\
\
The storage holds 1000 mB. An open Libation Spout drains it into the block below. Breaking the slab drops the items on it; the water and the stored Principles are lost.
In a vessel, an opposed pair never cures. The two Primals simply stay in the water together. I have not yet found what that does, but I will note it when I do.
*Silt against gleam, sap against ash. The tablets set them in pairs and say that the pairs strain against each other. The strain has a name, isfet, and the scribe does not write down what it does.*
Ash washes out of coal, charcoal, flint and bone. It is the Primal of what is burned, and shard and bitumen are made from it.
Opposed to **Sap**. Ash and sap never cure together.
*What the fire leaves behind is ash, and the tablets say it is the remainder of everything that was burned.*

- Coal: 50 mB
- Charcoal: 50 mB
- Flint: 50 mB
- Bone: 50 mB
- Rotten flesh: 25 mB, with 25 mB of sap
Gleam washes out of glass, glowstone dust, gold nuggets and feathers. It goes into myrrh and glaze in the light, and into unguent and kohl in the dark.
Opposed to **Silt**. Gleam and silt never cure together.
*Gleam is the light the tablets ask for, the brightness that is put into a thing and does not fade.*

- Glass: 50 mB
- Glowstone dust: 50 mB
- Gold nugget: 25 mB
- Feather: 25 mB
Sap is the Primal of growing things. It washes out of wheat, seeds, saplings and leaves, and rotten flesh gives it along with ash. It goes into loam and myrrh.
Opposed to **Ash**. Sap and ash never cure together.
*Sap is the green of the field, and the field does not grow without the labour of the gods.*

- Wheat: 50 mB
- Saplings (any): 50 mB
- Wheat seeds: 25 mB
- Leaves (any): 25 mB
- Rotten flesh: 25 mB, with 25 mB of ash
Silt washes out of dirt, clay balls, sand and cobblestone. It is the first Primal I can wash, and loam and mire are made from it.
Opposed to **Gleam**. Silt and gleam never cure together.
*The first thing the gods dug from the river was silt, and they set it under everything else. Whatever is laid in the mud is laid in silt.*

- Dirt: 50 mB
- Clay ball: 50 mB
- Sand: 50 mB
- Cobblestone: 50 mB
The clay by the river bears marks: wedges, rows of them, too regular to be chance. I have started copying them here. If they are words, someone meant them to last.
*In the beginning the gods laboured, and the labour was heavy. They dug the rivers. They bore the baskets. And they wept beneath the weight.*

Wood for the bones, quickened clay for the sinews. The body is made from the recipe above, and a golem is given its purpose once it stands. See [The Body](entry://principiamagica:principia/golemancy/the_body).

Clay holds a law, but law alone does not move. The old makers mixed in flesh, and I have only what the dead leave behind. Steep a clay ball with 25 mB of unguent in the Catch Trough, and for every 25 mB it gives back two quickened clay. See [Steeping](entry://principiamagica:principia/khemeia/steeping).

A clay phial holds 250 mB of one Principle. Empty phials, and phials holding exactly the same Principle and amount, stack up to 16. Select a Principle with crouch-scroll while the phial is empty.
\
\
Right-click a Principle container to pour the phial into it. Crouch-right-click a container to draw its Principles into the phial.
*The clay of the first makers lay dead until it drank. What it drinks is the flesh of the god, and the ghost in that flesh remembers the word. Let the clay drink, and it will hear.*

Right-click a Principle container to blot out the Principle selected on the HUD. Crouch-right-click it to purge every Principle it holds.
\
\
The sponge is reusable, so one sponge serves many vessels.
Every axiom is carved into a tablet first. The tablet is a stylus with two quickened clay. See [Processing Axioms](entry://principiamagica:principia/golemancy/axioms).

Rotten flesh is no food. But the dead keep something in it, and the tablets speak of flesh and clay in the same breath. I have been wondering whether one needs the other. I will look for it where the light does not reach.
*Something of life is left in the flesh of the dead. The tablets do not say it is good. They say only that it remembers, and that the clay will want it.*
A spout carries the water off the slab, and a tap lets a vessel drain. Both are small blocks that sit beside the block they serve, and they both open and close with an empty hand.
*The water runs down the carved lip and into the cup below. Whatever the water took from the offering, it carries on to the vessel.*

Place the spout on a side of the slab. It faces away from the slab. An empty-hand click opens or closes it, and so does a redstone signal.
\
\
An open spout drains 25 mB every 10 ticks into the block directly below it. That block must hold Principles: a Catch Trough, a Wabet Basin or a Steeping Jar. A comparator reads the slab's water.

The tap goes on a side of a Wabet Basin or a Steeping Jar, one tap to each vessel. It works like the spout: an empty-hand click or a redstone signal opens and closes it.
\
\
An open tap drains the vessel 25 mB every 10 ticks into the block below. A full basin empties in about 20 seconds. A comparator reads the vessel's fill.
The copied tablets say the clay remembers every mark pressed into it. I believe them now. Everything in this book is a mark I have seen and made, and I will keep to what I have actually observed.
*The reed is cut, the clay is wet, the word goes in. What is pressed in the clay does not leave it. The clay remembers.*
A cut reed would do, but copper holds its edge. With this I can carve the clay, and, if the tablets are right, command what the clay holds.
*The reed is cut, the clay is wet, the word goes in. What is pressed in the clay does not leave it.*

As a crafting tool, the stylus is never consumed: it returns to your grid after every recipe that uses it.
\
\
As a configuration tool, it selects a golem, carves, lifts and moves its work boundaries, and links its containers. See [Kudurru](entry://principiamagica:principia/golemancy/kudurru).
